articles.title: Pinterest Scraper in Go: Board RSS, Pin Pages, and a Saves Tracker in SQLite (2026)
articles.excerpt: Pinterest is quietly one of the best datasets for anyone working in e-commerce, home decor, food, or fashion. Saves are a pretty honest signal of what people actually want to buy or make, and they sho…
articles.body: Pinterest is quietly one of the best datasets for anyone working in e-commerce, home decor, food, or fashion. Saves are a pretty honest signal of what people actually want to buy or make, and they show up weeks before a trend hits other platforms. Getting that data out is a different story. In this post I'll build a small Go tool that: Reads the latest pins from any public board or profile Opens each pin and pulls out title, outbound link, domain, creation date, repins, and saves Stores a snapshot on every run in SQLite, so you can see which pins are picking up saves Everything here was tested against live Pinterest pages in October 2026. I'll also point out the parts that are flaky, because a few of them surprised me.

articles.title: How Do Mantle Bridge Payouts Handle Destination Reorgs?
articles.excerpt: A destination-chain reorg can erase a bridge credit for several blocks; on Ethereum, finality usually takes around 13–15 minutes, so a receipt alone is not an irreversible payout signal. For treasury…
articles.body: A destination-chain reorg can erase a bridge credit for several blocks; on Ethereum, finality usually takes around 13–15 minutes, so a receipt alone is not an irreversible payout signal. For treasury operations, treat source acceptance, destination inclusion and destination finality as separate states. A transfer can be valid on its source chain while its apparent credit is still reversible on the destination. A destination receipt is provisional until its block is stable A reorg replaces a chain’s recent canonical blocks, which can remove a transaction and its logs from the active history. The balance change then disappears from the recipient’s canonical state, even if an RPC endpoint previously returned a successful receipt.

articles.title: 23% of News Pages Have a Broken Link. Catch Yours Before Deploy
articles.excerpt: This article was written with AI assistance and reviewed by the author. In May 2024, Pew Research Center reported that 23% of news webpages in its sample contained at least one broken link, and 21% of…
articles.body: This article was written with AI assistance and reviewed by the author. In May 2024, Pew Research Center reported that 23% of news webpages in its sample contained at least one broken link, and 21% of government webpages did too [1]. Across a decade of Common Crawl snapshots, a quarter of pages that existed between 2013 and 2023 were already inaccessible by October 2023 [1]. Link rot is not a niche SEO footnote. It is a measurable property of the public web. Yet many static sites still discover 404s the hard way: after deploy, after a CDN purge, after a user files a ticket. Source review and local preview often miss the problems that only appear in the built output on a case-sensitive host. That is the gap static-link-sentinel is built for.

Keyword en ja es pt fr de ko chatgpt (posts/hour) 47.5 11.9 2.2 2.2 2.2 2.1 0.3 netflix (posts/hour) 51.1 3.9 3.5 2.6 3.2 1.5 0.1 English dominates, no surprise. But for "chatgpt", Japanese was a clear second, more than five times Spanish or Portuguese. That's a tiny sample on one day, so don't quote it as a market study.

articles.title: Trading Bot Success Rate: What the Number Really Means
articles.excerpt: A trading bot success rate, usually shown as the percentage of winning trades, tells you how often a bot wins, not whether it makes or loses money overall. To judge a bot honestly, you need its win ra…
articles.body: A trading bot success rate, usually shown as the percentage of winning trades, tells you how often a bot wins, not whether it makes or loses money overall. To judge a bot honestly, you need its win rate together with average win and loss size, trading costs, number of trades and drawdown, ideally measured over a forward test rather than only a backtest. This guide covers what "success rate" means, why high win rates can hide losing systems, and a simple process you can use to test any bot before trusting it with real capital. What "trading bot success rate" actually measures When a sales page says a bot has an "85% success rate," it almost always means: Win rate: winning trades divided by total trades.

articles.title: 2026 Privacy-Focused Personal Knowledge Manager Search: Cache Invalidation Under Load
articles.excerpt: When a private knowledge manager answers questions over PDFs, caching is a retrieval-quality decision before it is a latency trick. A cache hit can return an answer built from a document that was dele…
articles.body: When a private knowledge manager answers questions over PDFs, caching is a retrieval-quality decision before it is a latency trick. A cache hit can return an answer built from a document that was deleted, re-encrypted, or replaced. My default is to cache deterministic retrieval inputs and intermediate results, then re-check document version and access scope before generation. That keeps latency predictable without pretending stale context is harmless. Short answer: use versioned, scope-aware caches with short-lived result entries; invalidate by document revision, embedding configuration, and permission scope, and measure stale-hit rate alongside latency. How should a privacy-focused personal knowledge manager cache retrieval results?

articles.title: I measured my OCR pipeline on 36 old book scans. The phone-photo fix was one division.
articles.excerpt: I've been building a PDF-to-text tool that also has to cope with scanned pages. At some point "it works on my test PDFs" stopped meaning anything, so I set up a proper test: 36 public-domain book page…
articles.body: I've been building a PDF-to-text tool that also has to cope with scanned pages. At some point "it works on my test PDFs" stopped meaning anything, so I set up a proper test: 36 public-domain book pages from Wikimedia Commons (1700s to 1900s) in German, English, Spanish, French, Hindi and Portuguese, six per language. Wikisource has proofread transcriptions of these pages, so I could score the OCR output with character error rate (CER) instead of squinting at it. The engine is plain Tesseract 5 at 300 dpi. Everything below is about what happens around it. One page is out of the averages: a handwritten Portuguese manuscript. Tesseract produced nothing usable (CER 100 %), and no preprocessing trick changes that. The numbers below are over the other 35 printed pages. The baseline was fine.

articles.body: Larson didn’t do deep . He didn’t do inspirational. Many of his cartoons required you to think, but not because they were thoughtful in the lofty sense. They required thought because Larson’s work was brilliant, and you sometimes had to figure out what the punchline was. For example, this comic strip where an artist is painting a woman as a half-fly creature. You likely see the woman or the painting first, and you wonder why the artist is painting her that way. Only after inspecting the comic more closely do you see the dead fly on his glasses. Larson’s work often requires the reader to investigate something, but usually not in any kind of overly deep way.

articles.body: Every once in a while, I come across a line that feels bigger than the book that birthed it. The 1972 novel offers a very different kind of sci-fi ending than its myriad predecessors and successors.

articles.title: Rep. Ritchie Torres Introduces Legislation to Ensure Gamers Own Their Digital Games
articles.excerpt: Democratic Congressman Ritchie Torres is introducing legislation that aims to ensure you own your digital games, rather than having a license.
articles.body: Democratic Congressman Ritchie Torres is introducing legislation that aims to ensure you own your digital games, rather than merely buying a license that gives you permission to play them. The bill, known as The Power to the Players Act, would direct the Fedral Trade Commission (FTC) to establish regulations that would protect gamers and their digital libraries. In short, Torres wants to ensure that when you buy a digital game, you actually own it, as opposed to getting a license that can be revoked. Additionally, the bill would require online games to have offline functionality, so that when servers are shut down, the content can still be played by those who own the game.

articles.title: Astronomers discover the 1st ever green star, a cosmic zombie just in time for Halloween
articles.excerpt: Imagine if the sun could take on a spooky green glow for Halloween. Scientists have discovered that our star may go green if it turns into a cosmic zombie after its death in billions of years.
articles.body: How awesome would it be if the sun could take on a spooky green glow for Halloween? It turns out that scientists have discovered that our star may indeed go green, but only billions of years from now after its death — and only if it then starts eating planets like a cosmic zombie. That's possible because scientists have discovered that white dwarfs, the type of stellar remnants sun-sized stars leave behind when they die, can actually take on a range of colors including green if they snack on their rocky planets like cosmic cannibals. For stellar scientists, the colors of stars have always been indicative of their temperatures. Cool stars look orange, while stars like the sun look white , and the hottest stars glow pale blue.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 15, 1997: NASA launches Cassini-Hugyens probe on 7-year voyage to Saturn
articles.excerpt: On this day in space! Oct. 15, 1997: NASA launches Cassini-Hugyens probe on 7-year voyage to Saturn
articles.body: On Oct. 15, 1997, NASA launched the Cassini spacecraft on a mission to explore Saturn and its moons. It lifted off aboard a Titan 4B rocket from Cape Canaveral Air Force Station in Florida. It took almost seven years for the Cassini spacecraft to reach Saturn , with the spacecraft entering orbit around the ringed planet in 2004. Another smaller spacecraft called Huygens hitched a ride with Cassini, and it landed on Saturn's moon Titan in 2005. Cassini spent 13 years studying the Saturn system up close, and the mission lasted about 20 years before coming to an epic grand finale on Sept. 15, 2017 . articles.title: SpaceX launches classified mission for the US Space Force (video)
articles.excerpt: SpaceX launched a classified mission for the U.S. Space Force from California this evening (Oct. 15), on the 114th Falcon 9 mission of the year.
articles.body: SpaceX launched a classified mission for the U.S. Space Force from California this evening (Oct. 15). A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base today at 8:01 p.m. EDT (5:01 p.m. local time; 0001 GMT on Oct. 16), rising into clear blue skies above the Golden State's central coast. Such visibly striking launches are far from guaranteed; Vandenberg and its scenic surroundings are often blanketed by fog, making rocket watching in the area a dicey proposition. The Falcon 9's first stage rests on the deck of a drone ship shortly after launching the USSF-481 mission on Oct. 15, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) This evening's launch kicked off the USSF-481 mission, which is delivering mysterious payloads to an undisclosed location in the final frontier.
